objective: Prevent scientific and visualization code from treating event horizons, apparent horizons, MOTSs, marginally trapped tubes, dynamical horizons and isolated horizons as interchangeable.

primary_references.title: Quasi-local black hole horizons: recent advances
Event and Apparent Horizon Finders for 3+1 Numerical Relativity
primary_references.relevance: Global event-horizon reconstruction requires knowledge of the future spacetime; apparent horizons are found on Cauchy slices.

primary_references.title: BHaHAHA: A Fast, Robust Apparent Horizon Finder Library for Numerical Relativity
Horizon tracking for asynchronous parallel black hole simulations

invariants: A stationary Kerr r_plus formula is an analytic event/Killing-horizon property of the stationary solution, not a merger apparent-horizon finder.
An event horizon is a global causal boundary; its reconstruction depends on the future development and declared asymptotic/final boundary conditions.
An apparent horizon is slice-dependent and is normally the outermost MOTS on a declared Cauchy slice.
A MOTS is a two-surface satisfying a marginal null-expansion condition; it is not automatically an event horizon or a proven outermost apparent horizon.
A marginally trapped tube is a worldtube foliated by marginal surfaces; its branch and topology metadata are required.
Dynamical and isolated horizon classifications have distinct causal signatures and physical regimes.
Coordinate radii and visualization mesh geometry are not invariant surface observables; area and declared intrinsic multipoles are preferable for cross-chart comparisons.

caveats: Only claims the stationary Kerr solution property.
Does not describe a binary-merger horizon finder output.
Must include the future-time extent and the final boundary assumption.
A partial simulation cannot establish a complete global event horizon.

validation: outgoing null expansion is zero within a declared numerical tolerance
incoming null expansion has the declared negative sign
null-normal orientation and normalization are recorded
surface topology and branch identity are recorded
caveats: A MOTS does not by itself establish outermost status or event-horizon identity.

validation: linked MOTS exists on the declared slice
outermost status is either independently established or explicitly unknown
caveats: Slice dependence must be displayed; do not infer a global causal boundary.

validation: leaf continuity / branch transitions are recorded
worldtube signature is evaluated along the tube
caveats: Do not assume a smooth pair-of-pants topology or a single branch without verification.

validation: spacelike signature on the declared segment
area/flux balance convention and residual are recorded
caveats: Area increase is local and flux-related under the stated conditions; do not infer fluxes from area alone.
This is a quasi-local equilibrium boundary structure; it need not imply a global Killing symmetry throughout the exterior.

unsupported_or_ambiguous.policy: Do not silently coerce this state to apparent_horizon or event_horizon.

negative_controls: label a single-slice MOTS as an event horizon
omit Cauchy slice identity from an apparent-horizon record
omit future extent/final condition from an event-horizon reconstruction
flip outgoing/incoming null normals or metric signature
claim outermost status when multiple MOTSs exist
merge separate horizon branches across a topology change
compare coordinate radii across different charts as invariant areas
claim dynamical-horizon flux balance using an area time series alone
